requirements.article: BCBS 239 Principle 2 (Data architecture and IT infrastructure)
requirements.text: Roles and responsibilities for the ownership and quality of risk data are defined for both business and IT functions.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased from BCBS 239 (January 2013), principle level.

requirements.text: Risk data used as model input or output are accurate and reliable and are aggregated largely on an automated basis to minimise the probability of errors.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased from BCBS 239 (January 2013), principle level.

requirements.text: Risk data are reconciled with the bank's source systems, including accounting data where appropriate, to confirm their accuracy.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased from BCBS 239 (January 2013), principle level.

requirements.text: All risk data aggregation processes, automated and manual, are documented and explained, enabling data to be traced from source to report (data lineage).
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased from BCBS 239 (January 2013), principle level. Lineage expectations elaborated in the ECB Guide on effective risk data aggregation and risk reporting (May 2024).

requirements.text: An authoritative source is defined for each type of risk data used by the model.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased from BCBS 239 (January 2013), principle level.

requirements.text: Controls over risk data are as robust as those applied to accounting data, and data quality is measured and monitored against defined accuracy requirements, with manual workarounds documented and controlled.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased from BCBS 239 (January 2013), principle level.

requirements.text: All material risk data are captured and aggregated across the banking group, by business line, legal entity, asset type, industry and region as relevant to the risk.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased from BCBS 239 (January 2013), principle level.

requirements.text: Where risk data are not complete, the bank identifies and explains the gaps and assesses their impact on the reliability of the aggregated risk measures.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased from BCBS 239 (January 2013), principle level.

requirements.text: Aggregated risk data are available in a timely manner, meeting reporting frequency requirements in normal times and in stress or crisis situations.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased from BCBS 239 (January 2013), principle level.

requirements.text: Risk reports accurately and precisely convey aggregated risk data and are reconciled and validated before distribution.
requirements.verification_note: Paraphrased from BCBS 239 (January 2013), principle level.

requirements.text: The institution maintains documentation and evidence of continued compliance with the requirements of its internal approaches, supporting the competent authority's regular review, at least every three years.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRD text (Art. 101 unchanged in substance by CRD V/VI).

requirements.text: Where material deficiencies in the risk capture of an internal approach are identified, the institution rectifies them or implements the mitigating measures required, such as higher multiplication factors or capital add-ons.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRD text (Art. 101 unchanged in substance by CRD V/VI).

requirements.text: Where the institution's results diverge significantly from its peers, the institution provides the analysis needed to explain the divergence, including whether it reflects differences in underlying risk.
requirements.verification_note: Substance confirmed (investigation of significant divergence by the competent authority); paragraph number (78(3) or 78(4)) after CRD V amendments to be confirmed.

requirements.text: Internal ratings and default and loss estimates used in the own funds calculation play an essential role in the risk management and decision-making process and in the credit approval, internal capital allocation and corporate governance functions.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3. Use test; assessment methodology in Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/439 Art. 18–21.

requirements.text: The PD assigned to retail exposures is not lower than 0.1% for QRRE revolvers and not lower than 0.05% for all other retail exposures.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to retail PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: CRR3 retail PD input floors; values certain, point lettering within Art. 163(1) not verified.

requirements.text: The number of exposures in each retail grade or pool is sufficient for meaningful quantification and validation of loss characteristics, and the distribution of exposures and obligors avoids excessive concentrations.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to retail rating systems only.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3.

requirements.text: All relevant and current information is taken into account in assigning obligors and facilities to grades or pools; the less information available, the more conservative the assignment.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3.

requirements.text: The institution documents the situations in which human judgement may override the inputs or outputs of the assignment process and the personnel responsible for approving overrides.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3.

requirements.text: Overrides are recorded together with the responsible personnel, and the performance of exposures whose assignment was overridden is analysed, including an assessment of the performance of the responsible personnel.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3.

requirements.text: Retail assignments are updated at least annually, or the loss characteristics and delinquency status of each pool are reviewed at least annually together with a representative review of individual exposures within each pool.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to retail rating systems only.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3.

requirements.text: The institution has a process for vetting data inputs into the model, including an assessment of the accuracy, completeness and appropriateness of the data.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3.

requirements.text: The model is complemented by human judgement and oversight aimed at detecting and limiting errors from model weaknesses, using relevant information not considered by the model; how judgement and model results are combined is documented.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3.

requirements.text: The design and operational details of the rating systems are documented, evidencing compliance with the IRB requirements and covering portfolio differentiation, rating criteria, responsibilities, frequency of assignment reviews and management oversight.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3.

requirements.text: The definitions of default and loss used internally are documented and their consistency with the definitions in the CRR is demonstrated.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3.

requirements.text: For statistical models, the documentation gives a detailed outline of the theory, assumptions and mathematical and empirical basis of the assignment of estimates, and of the data sources used to estimate the model.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3.

requirements.text: Use of a third-party vendor model with proprietary technology does not exempt the institution from the documentation or any other IRB requirement.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3.

requirements.text: For retail, the institution stores the data used to allocate exposures to grades or pools, estimated PDs, LGDs and conversion factors per grade or pool, defaulted exposures with their grades or pools in the year before default, and realised LGDs and conversion factors.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to retail rating systems only.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3.

requirements.text: Default is recognised when the institution considers the obligor unlikely to pay its credit obligations to the institution, its parent or subsidiaries in full, without recourse to actions such as realising security.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3. Detailed in EBA/GL/2016/07 (see EXT-EBA-DOD).

requirements.text: Default is recognised when the obligor is more than 90 days past due on any material credit obligation to the institution, its parent or subsidiaries.
requirements.quote: the obligor is more than 90 days past due on any material credit obligation
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3. Detailed in EBA/GL/2016/07 (see EXT-EBA-DOD).

requirements.text: Materiality of past-due credit obligations is assessed against the threshold set by the competent authority, comprising an absolute and a relative component, in accordance with Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/171.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3. Threshold values per national competent authority / ECB Regulation (EU) 2018/1845.

requirements.text: The institution has documented policies on counting days past due, in particular on the re-ageing of facilities and the granting of extensions, amendments or deferrals, renewals, and the netting of existing accounts.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3.

requirements.text: Non-accrued status, a specific credit risk adjustment resulting from a significant perceived decline in credit quality, and the sale of a credit obligation at a material credit-related economic loss are treated as indications of unlikeliness to pay.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3. Detailed in EBA/GL/2016/07 (see EXT-EBA-DOD).

requirements.text: A distressed restructuring likely to result in a diminished financial obligation through material forgiveness or postponement of principal, interest or fees is treated as an indication of unlikeliness to pay.
requirements.verification_note: Substance confirmed; CRR3 amended point (d) (treatment of forbearance measures / diminished financial obligation) — exact current wording to be confirmed.

requirements.text: The institution filing for the obligor's bankruptcy or similar order, or the obligor seeking or being placed in bankruptcy or similar protection, is treated as an indication of unlikeliness to pay.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3.

requirements.text: Where external data are used that are not consistent with the institution's definition of default, appropriate adjustments are made to achieve broad equivalence with that definition.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3.

requirements.text: An obligor or facility is returned to non-defaulted status only when no default trigger continues to apply; a subsequent triggering of a default event is treated as a new default.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3.

requirements.text: Estimates of PD, LGD, conversion factors and EL incorporate all relevant data, information and methods and are derived from historical experience and empirical evidence, not purely from judgemental considerations.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the consolidated CRR text as amended by CRR3 (consolidated version 2026).

requirements.text: The less data the institution has, the more conservative its estimation.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the consolidated CRR text as amended by CRR3 (consolidated version 2026).

requirements.text: Estimates are representative of long-run experience.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the consolidated CRR text as amended by CRR3 (consolidated version 2026). Point (b) also requires a breakdown of loss experience by risk drivers.

requirements.text: Changes in lending practice or in the process for pursuing recoveries over the observation periods used for estimation are taken into account.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the consolidated CRR text as amended by CRR3 (consolidated version 2026).

requirements.text: The RDS is representative of the current portfolio (risk drivers and default-rate levels).
requirements.quote: the population of exposures represented in the data used for estimation
requirements.verification_note: Pilot requirement (text and article fixed). Art. 179(1)(d) representativeness confirmed against the consolidated CRR3 text; detailed representativeness analysis in EBA/GL/2017/16 section 5.

requirements.text: The economic or market conditions underlying the estimation data are relevant to current and foreseeable conditions.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the consolidated CRR text as amended by CRR3 (consolidated version 2026).

requirements.text: The number of exposures in the sample and the data period used for quantification are sufficient to provide confidence in the accuracy and robustness of the estimates.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the consolidated CRR text as amended by CRR3 (consolidated version 2026).

requirements.text: Data deficiencies are identified and linked to a Margin of Conservatism category.
requirements.verification_note: Pilot requirement (text and article fixed). CRR Art. 179(1)(f) confirmed against the consolidated CRR3 text; EBA/GL/2017/16 section 4.4 (MoC categories A–C). CRM-STD-101 is an internal reference not covered by this file.

requirements.text: Where different estimates are used for the calculation of risk weights and for internal purposes, this is documented and reasonable.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the consolidated CRR text as amended by CRR3 (consolidated version 2026).

requirements.text: Where pooled data are used, the rating systems and criteria of the pool members are similar to the institution's own, the pool is representative of the portfolio and the data are used consistently over time; the institution retains responsibility and in-house understanding.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the consolidated CRR text as amended by CRR3 (consolidated version 2026).

requirements.text: Internal data are the primary source for retail loss characteristics; external or pooled data or statistical models are used only where a strong link is demonstrated in assignment process and in risk profile and composition.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to retail PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the consolidated CRR text as amended by CRR3 (consolidated version 2026).

requirements.text: The RDS covers at least 5 years of historical data for retail PD estimation.
requirements.quote: at least five years for at least one source
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to retail PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: Pilot requirement (text and article fixed). Confirmed against the consolidated CRR3 text: minimum five-year observation period for at least one source.

requirements.text: The institution identifies and analyses expected changes of risk parameters over the life of retail credit exposures (seasoning effects).
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to retail PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the consolidated CRR text as amended by CRR3 (consolidated version 2026).

requirements.text: The institution has robust systems to validate the accuracy and consistency of rating systems, processes and the estimation of all relevant risk parameters, enabling a consistent and meaningful assessment of their performance.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3.

requirements.text: All material aspects of the rating and estimation processes are approved by the management body or a designated committee and by senior management, who possess a general understanding of the rating systems and of the associated management reports.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3.

requirements.text: Management reporting includes the risk profile by grade, migration across grades, parameter estimates per grade, and comparison of realised default rates (and, where applicable, realised LGDs and conversion factors) against expectations and stress-test outcomes.
requirements.verification_note: Confirmed against the CRR text; provision not materially amended by CRR3.

requirements.text: Historical data used for risk parameter estimation are adjusted, where possible, to the definition of default under these guidelines, including the materiality threshold for past due credit obligations.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to institutions using the IRB Approach (risk parameter estimation) only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: In regular reviews of estimates, the data window is extended (or justifiably moved) to include data collected under the new default definition, and the related MoC is reassessed until a sufficiently long homogeneous period exists.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to institutions using the IRB Approach (risk parameter estimation) only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.chapter: 4 Past due criterion — counting of days past due
requirements.text: Any amount of principal, interest or fee not paid at the date it was due is recognised as a past due credit obligation.
requirements.quote: where any amount of principal, interest or fee has not been paid at the date it was due
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.chapter: 4 Past due criterion — counting of days past due
requirements.text: Internal policies specify that, where the payment schedule has been modified, days past due are counted on the basis of the modified schedule.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.chapter: 4 Past due criterion — counting of days past due
requirements.text: Instalments changed, suspended or postponed under contractual rights or by law are not counted as past due, and the reasons for such changes or suspensions are analysed for indications of unlikeliness to pay.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.chapter: 4 Past due criterion — counting of days past due
requirements.text: Days past due counting is suspended for disputed obligations only where the dispute is before a court or other formal binding procedure or, for leasing, a complaint is confirmed by an independent unit.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.chapter: 4 Past due criterion — counting of days past due
requirements.text: Where days past due are calculated less often than daily, the date of default is set to the date on which the past due criterion was actually fulfilled.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.chapter: 4 Past due criterion — counting of days past due
requirements.text: Once the past due criterion is met, the obligor is classified as defaulted without additional expert judgement and all its exposures are defaulted, except under retail facility-level application or a technical past due situation.
requirements.quote: The classification of the obligor to a defaulted status should not be subject to additional expert judgement
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.chapter: 4 Past due criterion — counting of days past due
requirements.text: Technical past due situations are recognised only in the listed cases (institution data or system errors, payment execution failures, payment allocation time lags, specified factoring cases), excluding wrong credit decisions.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against EBA/GL/2016/07. Amended by EBA/GL/2026/05 (applies from 19.10.2026): point (d) (factoring) replaced; tolerance extended from 30 to 90 days and undisclosed/uninformed factoring cases moved here from paras 31-32. Requirement wording covers both versions.

requirements.chapter: 4 Past due criterion — counting of days past due
requirements.text: Technical past due situations are removed from the reference data set of defaulted exposures used for the estimation of risk parameters.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to institutions using the IRB Approach (risk parameter estimation) only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: The competent authority's materiality threshold is applied; a lower internal threshold is used only where shown to be a relevant UTP indication without excessive short-lived defaults, and is recorded as a separate UTP trigger.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: Unlikeliness-to-pay triggers are documented and applied consistently.
requirements.verification_note: Pilot record (section-level reference kept). Detailed basis: paras 35-65, in particular paras 58 and 64-65 (policies covering all exposure types, business lines, legal entities and locations).

requirements.text: An obligor is considered unlikely to pay where interest on its credit obligations is no longer recognised in the income statement due to a decrease in credit quality (non-accrued status).
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: Specific credit risk adjustments resulting from a significant perceived decline in credit quality are treated as UTP indications, whereas adjustments for incurred-but-not-reported losses are not.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: An exposure treated as impaired is an indication of unlikeliness to pay and the obligor is considered defaulted, regardless of whether specific credit risk adjustments are assigned.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: Exposures classified as credit-impaired (Stage 3) under IFRS 9 are considered defaulted, unless impairment results from payment delay and a listed exception applies (threshold not breached, technical past due, public sector treatment).
requirements.verification_note: Checked against EBA/GL/2016/07. Amended by EBA/GL/2026/05 (applies from 19.10.2026): point (a) (180 dpd discretion) deleted following CRR3; requirement lists only the remaining exceptions.

requirements.text: The reasons for each sale of credit obligations and related losses are analysed; a sale loss is treated as not credit-related only with appropriate, documented justification.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: A threshold of at most 5% is set for the credit-related economic loss on sale, L = (E - P)/E, and obligations sold with a loss above it are considered defaulted.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: Where a sale at a material credit-related loss precedes default identification, the moment of sale is the date of default, and after a partial sale all remaining exposures to the obligor are defaulted (except retail facility level).
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: For each forbearance measure (distressed restructuring), the diminished financial obligation (NPV0 - NPV1)/NPV0 at the original effective interest rate is calculated, and exposures above the threshold of at most 1% are defaulted.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against EBA/GL/2016/07. Amended by EBA/GL/2026/05 (applies from 19.10.2026): para 52 now refers to 'forbearance measure' instead of 'distressed restructuring' (CRR3 Art. 178(3)(d)); paras 49-50 deleted. 1% threshold confirmed.

requirements.text: Forborne exposures below the diminished-obligation threshold are assessed for other UTP indications, such as a large final lump sum, back-loaded or irregular schedule, significant grace period or repeated forbearance.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against EBA/GL/2016/07. Amended by EBA/GL/2026/05 (applies from 19.10.2026): para 53 replaced with 'forbearance measure' wording; indicators unchanged.

requirements.text: All exposures classified as forborne non-performing are classified as defaulted.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against EBA/GL/2016/07. Amended by EBA/GL/2026/05 (applies from 19.10.2026): para 54 replaced: forborne non-performing per CRR Arts 47a-47b classified as defaulted; the 2016 text also required any concession to a defaulted obligor to be treated as distressed restructuring.

requirements.text: UTP identification takes into account external information, including credit registers, macroeconomic indicators and public sources such as press articles and analyst reports.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: Internal policies specify when the default of one obligor in a group of connected clients has a contagious effect on other group entities, with a case-by-case assessment where not specified.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: For each indication of unlikeliness to pay, the identification method, internal and external information sources and monitoring frequency are defined.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.chapter: 6 Definition of default in external data
requirements.text: The default definition in external data used for estimation is verified against CRR Article 178 and the internal definition (dpd counting, materiality threshold, restructuring, SCRA, cure criteria), and sources, analysis and differences are documented.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to institutions using the IRB Approach (risk parameter estimation) only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.chapter: 6 Definition of default in external data
requirements.text: For each identified difference the direction of impact on default rates is assessed and the external data are adjusted or the difference shown negligible, demonstrating broad equivalence with the internal definition.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to institutions using the IRB Approach (risk parameter estimation) only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: Probation (cure) periods are applied before a facility returns to non-default status.
requirements.verification_note: Pilot record (section-level reference kept). Detailed minimum periods are captured in EBA-DOD-071a (3 months) and EBA-DOD-072 (1 year for forbearance).

requirements.text: A previously defaulted exposure is considered to have no default trigger only after at least 3 months have passed since the past due and UTP conditions ceased to be met.
requirements.quote: at least 3 months have passed since the moment that the conditions referred to in Articles 178(1)(b) and 178(3)
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: The obligor's behaviour and financial situation during the probation period are assessed, and the exposure stays defaulted until the improvement in credit quality is factual and permanent.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: Exposures defaulted due to distressed restructuring (forbearance) remain defaulted for at least one year from the latest of the restructuring measure, the default classification or the end of the grace period.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against EBA/GL/2016/07. Amended by EBA/GL/2026/05 (applies from 19.10.2026): para 72 replaced with 'forbearance measure' wording (default under CRR Art. 178(3)(d)); one-year period and start events unchanged.

requirements.text: Return to non-default after restructuring requires a material payment during the probation period, i.e. regular payments totalling the amount previously past due or written off.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: Return to non-default after restructuring also requires regular payments per the new schedule, no past due obligations, no UTP indications and no other doubt about full repayment, notably for back-loaded schedules.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: The effectiveness of return-to-non-default policies is monitored regularly through status changes, cure rates and multiple defaults, and the policies are revised where multiple defaults are extensive.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.chapter: 8 Consistency of the definition of default
requirements.text: The default of a single obligor is identified consistently for all its exposures across all relevant IT systems, legal entities of the group and geographical locations.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.chapter: 8 Consistency of the definition of default
requirements.text: Where legal impediments to intra-group client data exchange cause inconsistent default identification, the competent authority is informed and, for IRB, the materiality and impact on risk parameters are estimated.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.chapter: 8 Consistency of the definition of default
requirements.text: Where different default definitions are used, the scope of application of each is clearly specified and each is applied consistently to all exposures within its scope.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.chapter: 8 Consistency of the definition of default
requirements.text: Where a rating system's scope encompasses different default definitions, this is adequately reflected in the estimation of risk parameters.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to institutions using the IRB Approach (risk parameter estimation) only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: The level of application of the default definition (obligor or facility) for retail exposures reflects internal risk management practice, and the scope of each level is clearly specified and used consistently over time.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to retail exposures only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: Where retail default is applied at facility level, obligor-related UTP indications, such as bankruptcy, lead to all exposures to the obligor being treated as defaulted.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to retail exposures only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: Where retail default is applied at obligor level, internal policies set rules for joint credit obligations and contagion, including defaulting individual exposures when a joint obligation defaults unless para 97 exceptions apply.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to retail exposures only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: Where retail default is applied at obligor level, the materiality threshold is applied at obligor level, with a joint obligor treated as a separate obligor in the threshold calculation.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to retail exposures only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: Automatic default identification processes, such as counting of days past due, are performed on a daily basis.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: Manual default identification processes (external sources, watch lists, forborne exposure lists, SCRA) are updated with a frequency that guarantees timely identification of default.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: It is regularly verified that all forborne non-performing exposures are classified as defaulted, and forborne performing exposures are regularly analysed for indications of unlikeliness to pay.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against EBA/GL/2016/07. Amended by EBA/GL/2026/05 (applies from 19.10.2026): para 107 replaced (drops 'distressed restructuring' wording, cross-refers to paras 51-55); obligation unchanged.

requirements.text: All exposures to a defaulted obligor are flagged as defaulted in all relevant IT systems without undue delay, and any recording delays do not cause errors in the data used for risk quantification.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.text: The operationalisation of every indication of default is documented in detail, including the process, sources of information and responsibilities for its identification.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2016/07; paragraph not changed by amending Guidelines EBA/GL/2026/05 (apply from 19.10.2026).

requirements.chapter: 4.1 Range of application of rating systems
requirements.text: The same definition of default is applied to the same historical observations used in the different PD and LGD models of a rating system.
requirements.quote: institutions should apply the same definition of default for the same historical observations used in different models
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.text: Data used in model development and as model inputs in application are sufficiently precise to avoid material distortions of grade or pool assignment and contain no biases that make them unfit for purpose.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.text: Every exclusion from the RDS has a documented reason.
requirements.verification_note: Pilot record (section-level reference kept). Specific basis: para 72 (documentation of data cleansing and exclusions in the one-year default rate calculation) and Art. 32(3)(b) RTS on IRB assessment methodology.

requirements.text: Every exclusion is quantified (facilities, share of population, defaults).
requirements.verification_note: Pilot record (section-level reference kept). Specific basis: para 72(b) (reasons and quantity of exclusions for retail PD models) and para 72(a) (list of excluded observations for non-retail).

requirements.text: Treatment of missing values and outliers is documented and justified.
requirements.verification_note: Pilot record. The GL contain no paragraph explicitly on missing values and outliers; substance derives from paras 15-16 (data quality), 37(a)(v) (missing risk driver data as Category A deficiency) and 70(c). Confirm the section-level reference is acceptable.

requirements.text: Internal policies specify the statistical tests and metrics used to assess data representativeness, separately for data used in risk differentiation and for data underlying risk quantification.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.text: Where external or pooled data are used, sufficient information is obtained from the data providers to assess their representativeness for the institution's own portfolios and processes.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.chapter: 4.2.3 Representativeness of data for model development
requirements.text: The representativeness of the development data for the application portfolio is analysed in terms of scope of application, definition of default, distribution of relevant risk characteristics, and lending standards and recovery policies.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.chapter: 4.2.3 Representativeness of data for model development
requirements.text: The definition of default underlying the development data is consistent over time: historical data are adjusted where the definition changed, and the definition in each data source is analysed separately.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.chapter: 4.2.3 Representativeness of data for model development
requirements.text: Material differences in key risk characteristics between the development sample and the application portfolio, identified with the statistical tests specified in policy, are addressed (e.g. other sample, subset of observations or additional risk drivers).
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.chapter: 4.2.3 Representativeness of data for model development
requirements.text: Significant changes in lending standards, recovery policies or the legal environment over the historical observation period are analysed by comparing RDS data before and after the change.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.chapter: 4.2.3 Representativeness of data for model development
requirements.text: The PD development dataset contains a sufficient number of defaulted and non-defaulted observations, and any difference from the default proportion of the application portfolio is documented.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.text: The comparability of data used to calculate long-run average default rates or LGDs is analysed for scope, default definition, risk characteristics, current and foreseeable economic conditions, and lending and recovery standards.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.text: The current definition of default is compared with those underlying the calibration data; where it changed during the observation period, each past definition is analysed separately as for external data under the DoD guidelines.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.text: The impact of exclusions on representativeness is analysed.
requirements.verification_note: Pilot record (section-level reference kept). Specific basis: paras 25, 31 and 34 (representativeness and resulting adjustment/MoC); para 218(b)(ii) requires performance review without development exclusions.

requirements.text: All deficiencies leading to bias or to uncertainty not captured by the general estimation error are identified and classified as Category A (data and methodological) or Category B (changes and other sources of uncertainty).
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.text: The RDS contains the values of risk drivers at appropriate points in time, reflecting their dynamics and update frequency and, for defaulted obligors, throughout the year prior to default.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.text: The model or assignment process applies an adequate, conservative adjustment where financial statements or credit bureau information used as relevant risk drivers are older than 24 months.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.chapter: 5.3.1-5.3.3 PD — one-year and observed average default rates
requirements.text: Observations are excluded from one-year default rates only if wrongly classified as defaults (numerator only) or wrongly assigned to the model's scope (numerator and denominator).
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.chapter: 5.3.1-5.3.3 PD — one-year and observed average default rates
requirements.text: The one-year default rate denominator comprises non-defaulted obligors with any on- or off-balance credit obligation at the start of the period; the numerator those with at least one default during the year.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.chapter: 5.3.1-5.3.3 PD — one-year and observed average default rates
requirements.text: Grade assignment for default rate calculation takes overrides into account but excludes substitution effects of credit risk mitigation and ex post conservative adjustments.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.chapter: 5.3.1-5.3.3 PD — one-year and observed average default rates
requirements.text: One-year default rates are also calculated for obligors within the model's scope that had no rating at the start of the observation period (missing ratings).
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.chapter: 5.3.1-5.3.3 PD — one-year and observed average default rates
requirements.text: Obligors that migrate to another grade, model or approach, or whose obligations are sold, written off or repaid during the period, remain in the default rate calculation, and any resulting bias is analysed.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.chapter: 5.3.1-5.3.3 PD — one-year and observed average default rates
requirements.text: Each defaulted obligor is counted only once in the numerator and denominator of a one-year default rate, even if it defaulted more than once in that period.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.text: The historical observation period includes observations beyond the most recent five years where needed to reflect the likely range of variability of default rates.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.chapter: 5.3.5 PD — calibration to the long-run average
requirements.text: The calibration sample of each calibration segment is stored and described in the PD model documentation.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.text: The framework for regular review of estimates defines the minimum scope and frequency of analyses, predefined metrics, thresholds and significance levels, and predefined actions for adverse results.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.text: The at least annual review analyses representativeness of the RDS used for quantification and for development against the application portfolio, including portfolio changes and structural breaks.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.text: Data adjustment and exclusion policies are applied consistently across the datasets used in the review of estimates, and any differences are justified and do not distort the review results.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the official EN text of EBA/GL/2017/16 (EBA website PDF).

requirements.text: The validation function performs internal validation at each level (consolidated, sub-consolidated, individual) at which the rating system is approved or approval is sought.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against EBA/REP/2023/29 (PDF).

requirements.text: The validation report describes all tests performed and the validation samples used, including sizes, comparison with the application portfolio and overlap with the RDS.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against EBA/REP/2023/29 (PDF).

requirements.text: The validation function assesses whether IRB metrics (realised DR, economic loss and realised LGD, realised CF) follow regulatory definitions and compares its own metrics with those of the CRCU.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against EBA/REP/2023/29 (PDF).

requirements.text: The validation function assesses the comprehensiveness of the rating assignment, including the materiality of missing and outdated ratings in the application portfolio and the CRCU's resolution plan.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against EBA/REP/2023/29 (PDF).

requirements.text: The validation function analyses representativeness of the development sample against the application portfolio for scope, definition of default, risk characteristics, lending standards and recovery policies.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against EBA/REP/2023/29 (PDF).

requirements.text: The validation function reviews the input data used for risk quantification, including RDS completeness and data cleansing, to ensure that uncertainty from identified deficiencies is covered by MoC.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against EBA/REP/2023/29 (PDF).

requirements.text: The validation function challenges the choices underlying the long-run average default rate, in particular the length of the historical period used.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD models only.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against EBA/REP/2023/29 (PDF).

requirements.text: The validation function back-tests PD estimates against realised default rates per grade or pool, using the longest available history and, as best practice, sub-periods.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD models only.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against EBA/REP/2023/29 (PDF).

requirements.text: The validation function forms an opinion on data quality dimensions and processes and checks whether identified deficiencies bias the risk parameters or require MoC.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against EBA/REP/2023/29 (PDF).

requirements.chapter: Specific challenges – external data and outsourcing
requirements.text: Where external data are used, the validation function assesses their representativeness for the application portfolio, challenges their appropriateness and reviews the Category A MoC.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against EBA/REP/2023/29 (PDF).

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles, para 4
requirements.text: Model documentation enables a qualified third party to independently understand the methodology, assumptions, limitations and use of the model and to replicate its development and implementation.
requirements.quote: All internal models should be documented to allow a qualified third party to independently understand the methodology, assumptions, limitations and use of the model
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles, para 9
requirements.text: Sound data governance practices, as set out in chapter 3.2 of the ECB Guide on effective risk data aggregation and risk reporting, are in place for all data used as model inputs.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles, para 11
requirements.text: Where the target variable is determined by human judgement (e.g. unlikeliness-to-pay flags), a data governance process with clear labelling guidelines and regular analyses ensures no systematic labelling differences between individuals.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles, para 13
requirements.text: Each internal model undergoes a regular complexity assessment that classifies it by complexity and explicitly identifies models labelled highly complex (e.g. due to ML techniques) or dynamic.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles, para 18
requirements.text: The internal model and its estimates are subject to an initial validation (new models, material changes and extensions) and subsequently to an annual internal validation.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Overarching principles, para 79
requirements.chapter: Implementation of changed or extended models
requirements.text: An approved material model change or extension is implemented within three months of notification of the permission, unless an exception has been requested and granted.
requirements.quote: The ECB generally expects this time frame to be no longer than three months from the date of the notification.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para 26
requirements.text: Material aspects of the rating and estimation processes are approved by the management body (or a designated committee) and by senior management.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to IRB rating systems only.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para 52(h)(iii)
requirements.text: The validation analyses representativeness of the development data for actual obligors or exposures, including range of application, changes to the definition of default, and lending standards or workout procedures.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to IRB rating systems only.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para 74
requirements.text: Internal ratings and default and loss estimates are used, as formalised in internal policies, in the approval, restructuring and renewal of credit facilities, lending policies and monitoring of obligors and exposures.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to IRB rating systems only.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para 90(b)
requirements.text: The override policy defines the maximum extent of overrides (e.g. maximum notches and maximum share of overridden exposures) and is more restrictive for positive than for negative overrides.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to IRB rating systems only.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para 101
requirements.text: In case of doubt, extensions and changes are assigned to the category of highest potential materiality.
requirements.quote: in case of doubt institutions shall assign extensions and changes to the category of the highest potential materiality
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to IRB rating systems only.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para 137
requirements.text: Data quality standards are defined for all model data inputs at each life-cycle stage for completeness, accuracy, consistency, timeliness, uniqueness, validity, availability and traceability.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to IRB rating systems only.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para 140
requirements.text: Data quality checks and controls operate from data entry to reporting and include reconciliations across and within systems, including between accounting and IRB data.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to IRB rating systems only.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para 154
requirements.text: When the days-past-due criterion is met, the default flag is activated for all affected exposures at the onset of the 91st consecutive day of material arrears; 'months in arrears' proxies are not used.
requirements.quote: at the onset of the 91st consecutive day after the materiality threshold is exceeded for the first time
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to IRB rating systems only.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para 174
requirements.text: Where external or pooled data follow a different definition of default, the institution fully understands that definition and demonstrates representativeness or adjusts the data to achieve broad equivalence.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to IRB rating systems only.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para 178
requirements.text: After a change to the definition of default, risk differentiation is demonstrated on a time series of realised default rates (or LGD/CCF) reflecting the new definition; otherwise the model is redeveloped.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to IRB rating systems only.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para 185
requirements.text: Where several data sources are used for risk quantification, common obligors are identified so that each counts only once in one-year default rates, or the resulting bias is analysed and reflected.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to IRB rating systems only.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para 187
requirements.text: Where representativeness of external data cannot be sufficiently proven, the institution shows that model performance does not deteriorate, estimates are not biased and an appropriate MoC is applied.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to IRB rating systems only.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para 207(b)
requirements.text: Risk differentiation is demonstrated on time series of realised default rates per grade or pool under different economic conditions.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para 234
requirements.chapter: Probability of default – use of external data
requirements.text: Where external or pooled data complement internal data, the internal-only LRA default rate is compared with the average PD before MoC; material segment-level or systematic grade-level differences indicate bias.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para 236(a)
requirements.text: The historical observation period for the LRA default rate contains at least the five most recent years, with any additional relevant years added as a continuous time span.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models – credit risk, LRA calibration
requirements.text: The observation period covers a representative mix of good and bad years, including a downturn.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: Pilot record; id, text and article kept as seeded. Substance maps to Credit risk para 236(b)–(d) (v4.0). The guide requires a representative mix of good and bad years (bad years defined via adverse economic indicators); 'downturn' is pilot wording, not the guide's term.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para 236(d)(i)
requirements.text: Where default rates correlate significantly with economic indicators, a documented criterion classifies years as good or bad, with bad years showing actually adverse indicator values.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para 236(d)(ii)-(iii)
requirements.text: The proportion of bad years in the historical observation period is not smaller than the reference proportion computed over the last 20 years of the economic indicator series.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para 236(d)(iv)
requirements.text: The institution verifies whether the maximum observed one-year default rate is included in the historical observation period and documents and justifies any exclusion.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text.

requirements.article: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para 237
requirements.text: At calibration-segment level, the LRA default rate before MoC is compared with a reference LRA default rate (best practice period 2008–2018); a lower LRA is justified or revised.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: Paragraph number and substance checked against the ECB guide to internal models, July 2025 (v4.0), PDF text. Para 238: the reference LRA DR guides the assessment but is not a quantification floor.

requirements.text: The validation tools are applied separately to each rating system approved at the start of the observation period, covering all customers or facilities within its range of application.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: The validation tools use the one-year observation period of the internal validation, with the annual end date kept constant across reporting years.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: Portfolio information (RWEA, EAD, number of customers or facilities, number of grades, number of defaults) is reported for the beginning and end of the observation period.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: Rating process statistics report customers with outdated ratings or financial statements, transferred ratings and process-deficiency exclusions relative to portfolio size M, with their PDs and defaults.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD models only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: The relative frequency of customers with overrides in the validation sample (M_def/N) is reported at portfolio level.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD models only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: PD calibration is tested with a one-sided Jeffreys test at portfolio and rating-grade level, reporting the Beta(D+1/2, N−D+1/2) distribution function evaluated at the PD as p-value.
requirements.quote: the PD applied in the portfolio/rating grade at the beginning of the relevant observation period is greater than the true one
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD models only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: Discriminatory power is tested by comparing the current AUC with the AUC at initial validation/development, using S = (AUCinit − AUCcurr)/s and p-value 1 − Φ(S).
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD models only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: Customer migrations over the observation period are summarised with the upper and lower matrix weighted bandwidth (MWB) statistics at portfolio level.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD models only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: Stability of the migration matrix is assessed with pairwise z-tests on the monotonicity of off-diagonal transition frequencies for each rating grade.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD models only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: Concentration in rating grades is assessed with the Herfindahl index, testing the current coefficient of variation against that at initial validation (number-weighted; exposure-weighted HI also reported).
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD models only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against ECB 'Instructions for reporting the validation results of internal models – IRB Pillar I models for credit risk' (February 2019).

requirements.text: Personal data used for model development and application are processed lawfully, fairly and in a transparent manner in relation to the data subject.
requirements.quote: processed lawfully, fairly and in a transparent manner in relation to the data subject
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) 2016/679 text. Fairness includes avoiding unjustified discriminatory effects of profiling (Recital 71).

requirements.text: Personal data are collected for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes and are not further processed, including for model development, in a manner incompatible with those purposes.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) 2016/679 text.

requirements.text: Personal data use is minimised and covered by a DPIA.
requirements.verification_note: Pilot requirement (text and article fixed). Checked against Reg. (EU) 2016/679 text. Covers data minimisation (Art. 5(1)(c)) and the DPIA duty (Art. 35); PRIV-POL-001 is the bank's internal privacy policy reference. Seed rationale: RDS contains personal data.

requirements.text: Personal data are accurate and, where necessary, kept up to date, and inaccurate personal data are erased or rectified without delay.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) 2016/679 text.

requirements.text: Personal data in model development and reference data sets are kept in identifiable form no longer than necessary for the purposes, with defined retention periods.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) 2016/679 text. Longer retention is possible for statistical purposes subject to Art. 89(1) safeguards; reconcile with CRR data-history requirements for IRB models.

requirements.text: Each processing purpose in the model lifecycle (development, validation, application) has a documented lawful basis under Art. 6(1).
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) 2016/679 text. Typical bases: contract (6(1)(b)), legal obligation (6(1)(c)), legitimate interest (6(1)(f)) with balancing test.

requirements.text: Where personal data collected for another purpose are reused for model development without consent or a legal basis in law, a documented compatibility assessment is performed considering the Art. 6(4)(a)-(e) factors.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) 2016/679 text.

requirements.text: Special categories of personal data (such as health, ethnic origin, religion) are not processed in model data unless an exception under Art. 9(2) applies and is documented.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) 2016/679 text. Check also inferred special-category data (e.g. from transaction descriptions). AI Act bias-detection basis: see AIA-10-5.

requirements.chapter: Data protection by design and by default (Art. 25)
requirements.text: Appropriate technical and organisational measures, such as pseudonymisation, are designed into the model data pipeline to implement data protection principles effectively, both at design time and during processing.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) 2016/679 text.

requirements.chapter: Data protection by design and by default (Art. 25)
requirements.text: By default, only personal data necessary for each specific purpose are processed, as regards amount collected, extent of processing, storage period and accessibility.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) 2016/679 text. Distinct from REQ-D25: addresses default settings of systems and access to model data.

requirements.text: The DPIA contains a systematic description of the processing and purposes, an assessment of necessity and proportionality, an assessment of risks to data subjects, and the measures envisaged to address those risks.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) 2016/679 text. A DPIA is mandatory for systematic and extensive evaluation based on automated processing including profiling (Art. 35(3)(a)), e.g. credit scoring.

requirements.text: Rating system documentation is complete, sufficiently detailed, up to date, approved at the appropriate management level and subject to version control, so that the competent authority can assess compliance.
requirements.verification_note: Article number and title checked against the table of contents of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/439; obligation paraphrased at article level from the assessment criteria.

requirements.text: Where a third party is involved in the design, development, data provision or operation of a rating system, the institution retains full responsibility and sufficient in-house understanding, and documents the third-party involvement.
requirements.verification_note: Article number and title checked against the table of contents of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/439; obligation paraphrased at article level from the assessment criteria.

requirements.text: The validation covers all rating systems and all their components, including data, model design, risk quantification, assignment processes and use, and the institution's full validation cycle is complete and performed with appropriate frequency.
requirements.verification_note: Article number and title checked against the table of contents of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/439; obligation paraphrased at article level from the assessment criteria.

requirements.text: Validation conclusions, findings and recommendations are reported to senior management and the management body or designated committee, and are addressed through a documented remediation process with follow-up.
requirements.verification_note: Article number and title checked against the table of contents of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/439; obligation paraphrased at article level from the assessment criteria.

requirements.text: The management body and senior management approve all material aspects of the rating systems, understand their design and operation, and are informed of material changes, exceptions and deficiencies.
requirements.verification_note: Article number and title checked against the table of contents of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/439; obligation paraphrased at article level from the assessment criteria.

requirements.text: Internal ratings and risk parameters used for own funds are applied in risk management, decision-making and the credit approval process, including limits, monitoring and reporting of credit risk.
requirements.verification_note: Article number and title checked against the table of contents of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/439; obligation paraphrased at article level from the assessment criteria.

requirements.text: Where risk parameters used for internal purposes differ from those used for own funds requirements, the differences are documented and justified, and the internal parameters are consistent with the IRB parameters.
requirements.verification_note: Article number checked; whether the justification of differing internal parameters sits in Art. 18 or Art. 19 to be confirmed.

requirements.chapter: Assignment of exposures to grades or pools
requirements.text: The assignment process has integrity: ratings are approved independently, updated timely and at least annually, and overrides are governed, recorded and monitored.
requirements.verification_note: Article number and title checked against the table of contents of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/439; obligation paraphrased at article level from the assessment criteria.

requirements.text: The default triggers of CRR Art. 178, including days-past-due and unlikeliness-to-pay indications, are implemented and applied consistently across all relevant entities, systems and portfolios.
requirements.verification_note: Article number and title checked against the table of contents of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/439; obligation paraphrased at article level from the assessment criteria.

requirements.text: The process for identifying defaults is robust, timely and effective, with automated identification where possible, documented manual processes, and controls ensuring completeness of default identification.
requirements.verification_note: Article number and title checked against the table of contents of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/439; obligation paraphrased at article level from the assessment criteria.

requirements.text: Reclassification of defaulted exposures to non-default status follows documented policies and is applied only when no default trigger continues to apply.
requirements.verification_note: Article number and title checked against the table of contents of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/439; obligation paraphrased at article level from the assessment criteria.

requirements.text: The documentation of each rating system covers its rationale, design and operational details, including the model, risk quantification, data, assignment process and use, completely enough for a third party to understand it.
requirements.verification_note: Article number and title checked against the table of contents of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/439; obligation paraphrased at article level from the assessment criteria.

requirements.text: Data used to develop statistical models are representative of the institution's portfolio, of adequate quality and sufficient in length and depth.
requirements.verification_note: Article number and title checked against the table of contents of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/439; obligation paraphrased at article level from the assessment criteria.

requirements.text: Human judgement used in model development and in the application of the model is justified, documented and its impact monitored.
