requirements.verification_note: Article number and title checked against the table of contents of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/439; obligation paraphrased at article level from the assessment criteria.

requirements.text: Data used for risk quantification are representative, complete and of sufficient length, and any data deficiencies are identified and treated.
requirements.verification_note: Article number and title checked against the table of contents of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/439; obligation paraphrased at article level from the assessment criteria.

requirements.text: The institution has a framework to identify deficiencies in data and methods, apply appropriate adjustments and quantify a margin of conservatism commensurate with the expected range of estimation errors.
requirements.verification_note: Article number and title checked against the table of contents of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/439; obligation paraphrased at article level from the assessment criteria.

requirements.text: The historical observation period used for PD estimation meets the minimum length requirements and includes a longer period where relevant data are available.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD estimation only.
requirements.verification_note: Article number and title checked against the table of contents of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/439; obligation paraphrased at article level from the assessment criteria.

requirements.chapter: Exposure classes, stress testing and own funds calculation
requirements.text: Exposures assigned to the retail exposure class meet the retail criteria, including the monitoring of thresholds and the management of exposures on a pooled basis.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to retail exposures only.
requirements.verification_note: Article number and title checked against the table of contents of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/439; obligation paraphrased at article level from the assessment criteria.

requirements.text: Data used in the rating systems are documented, including a data dictionary and data lineage, and data quality is reported to the relevant management levels.
requirements.verification_note: Article number checked; specific documentation elements (data dictionary, lineage) paraphrased and to be confirmed against the text.

requirements.text: Default is defined as > 90 dpd above the materiality threshold (EUR 100 absolute and 1% relative) or unlikeliness to pay.
requirements.verification_note: Pilot record (text and article kept). Imprecise for non-retail: EUR 100 is the maximum absolute component for retail (Art. 1(2)); for non-retail the maximum is EUR 500 (Art. 2(2)), and the levels applied are those set by the competent authority (for ECB-supervised institutions EUR 100 / EUR 500 and 1%).

requirements.text: The default definition for retail exposures uses the single materiality threshold set by the competent authority for all institutions in its jurisdiction.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to retail exposures only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the as-adopted text of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/171 (OJ version via legislation.gov.uk). The RTS addresses competent authorities; the requirement states the resulting obligation for the institution's default definition.

requirements.text: Where the retail default definition is applied at the level of an individual credit facility, the separate facility-level threshold set by the competent authority, if any, is applied.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to retail exposures only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the as-adopted text of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/171 (OJ version via legislation.gov.uk). The RTS addresses competent authorities; the requirement states the resulting obligation for the institution's default definition.

requirements.text: The absolute component is compared with the sum of all amounts past due owed by the obligor to the institution, its parent undertaking or any of its subsidiaries, and does not exceed EUR 100 for retail exposures.
requirements.quote: The maximum amount shall not exceed 100 EUR or the equivalent of that amount in the relevant national currency.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to retail exposures only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the as-adopted text of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/171 (OJ version via legislation.gov.uk). The RTS addresses competent authorities; the requirement states the resulting obligation for the institution's default definition.

requirements.article: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/171 Arts 1(2), third subparagraph, and 2(2)
requirements.text: The relative component is calculated as the credit obligation past due divided by the total on-balance-sheet exposures to the obligor of the institution, parent and subsidiaries, excluding equity exposures.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the as-adopted text of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/171 (OJ version via legislation.gov.uk). The RTS addresses competent authorities; the requirement states the resulting obligation for the institution's default definition. Same calculation applies to non-retail via Art. 2(2).

requirements.article: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/171 Arts 1(2), third subparagraph, and 4
requirements.text: The relative component applied equals the level set by the competent authority, which lies between 0% and 2.5% and is 1% unless the authority has substantiated a different level.
requirements.quote: The percentage shall be between 0 % and 2,5 % and shall be set at 1 %
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the as-adopted text of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/171 (OJ version via legislation.gov.uk). The RTS addresses competent authorities; the requirement states the resulting obligation for the institution's default definition.

requirements.text: Under facility-level application for retail, the amount past due and the total on-balance-sheet exposure in the threshold test refer only to the single credit facility concerned.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to retail exposures only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the as-adopted text of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/171 (OJ version via legislation.gov.uk). The RTS addresses competent authorities; the requirement states the resulting obligation for the institution's default definition.

requirements.text: A retail obligor (or facility) is defaulted under the past due criterion when both the absolute and the relative components are exceeded for 90 consecutive days.
requirements.quote: both the limit expressed as the absolute component of the materiality threshold and the limit expressed as the relative component of that threshold are exceeded
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to retail exposures only.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the as-adopted text of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/171 (OJ version via legislation.gov.uk). The RTS addresses competent authorities; the requirement states the resulting obligation for the institution's default definition. The alternative of 180 consecutive days in the RTS relied on the Art. 178(1)(b) CRR discretion that CRR3 removed, so only 90 days is reflected.

requirements.text: The days-past-due counter starts on the first day on which both threshold components are exceeded and restarts when either component is no longer exceeded.
requirements.verification_note: Derived from the 'consecutive days' wording of Arts 1(5) and 2(4) (addressed to competent authorities); the RTS does not spell out the counter mechanics explicitly. Confirm interpretation and article attribution.

requirements.chapter: Arts 5-6 Currency and date of application
requirements.text: Where the absolute component is set in a currency other than the euro, the threshold in that currency is applied unchanged even if exchange-rate movements push its euro equivalent above EUR 100 or EUR 500.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against the as-adopted text of Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/171 (OJ version via legislation.gov.uk). The RTS addresses competent authorities; the requirement states the resulting obligation for the institution's default definition.

requirements.chapter: Arts 5-6 Currency and date of application
requirements.text: The regulatory materiality threshold is applied from the date of application set by the competent authority, and the default flags in the RDS identify from which date it was applied.
requirements.verification_note: Art. 6 (as adopted) lets the competent authority set the date of application, no later than 31 December 2020 as regards Standardised Approach institutions. The second clause (RDS flagging) is a practical derivation, not literal text. Check the consolidated EUR-Lex text for later amendments.

requirements.text: Every change to the range of application of a rating system or to a rating system is classified either as material (requiring prior permission, CRR Art. 143(3)) or as other change requiring notification.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) No 529/2014, OJ L 148, 20.5.2014, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2015/942 (IRB provisions unchanged by that amendment). EBA/RTS/2026/05 (final draft amending RTS under CRR3 Art. 143(5), 30.3.2026, not yet in the OJ) keeps the substance.

requirements.text: Non-material changes are further classified as requiring notification before implementation (ex ante) or after implementation (ex post).
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) No 529/2014, OJ L 148, 20.5.2014, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2015/942 (IRB provisions unchanged by that amendment). EBA/RTS/2026/05 (final draft amending RTS under CRR3 Art. 143(5), 30.3.2026, not yet in the OJ) keeps the substance.

requirements.text: The quantitative impact of a change on risk-weighted exposure amounts is assessed using the most recent data available.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) No 529/2014, OJ L 148, 20.5.2014, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2015/942 (IRB provisions unchanged by that amendment).

requirements.text: Where a precise impact assessment is not feasible, the impact is assessed on a representative sample or with other reliable inference methodologies, and the approach is documented.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) No 529/2014, OJ L 148, 20.5.2014, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2015/942 (IRB provisions unchanged by that amendment).

requirements.text: A material change is not split into several changes or extensions of lower materiality.
requirements.quote: One material extension or change shall not be split into several changes or extensions of lower materiality.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) No 529/2014, OJ L 148, 20.5.2014, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2015/942 (IRB provisions unchanged by that amendment). CRR3: EBA/RTS/2026/05 (final draft amending RTS under CRR Art. 143(5), 30.3.2026, not yet adopted in the OJ at time of authoring) adds that simultaneous modifications and modifications of the same nature are assessed as one change, with phased implementation plans subject to notification. Re-verify once the amending Regulation is published.

requirements.text: In case of doubt, a change is assigned to the category of highest potential materiality.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) No 529/2014, OJ L 148, 20.5.2014, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2015/942 (IRB provisions unchanged by that amendment). EBA/RTS/2026/05 (final draft amending RTS under CRR3 Art. 143(5), 30.3.2026, not yet in the OJ) keeps the substance.

requirements.text: After permission of a material change, own funds requirements are calculated on the approved change from the date specified in the permission; non-implementation on that date requires a new permission applied for without undue delay.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) No 529/2014, OJ L 148, 20.5.2014, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2015/942 (IRB provisions unchanged by that amendment). EBA/RTS/2026/05 (final draft amending RTS under CRR3 Art. 143(5), 30.3.2026, not yet in the OJ) keeps the substance.

requirements.article: Reg. (EU) No 529/2014 Art. 4(1)(a); Annex I, Part I, Section 1, point 1
requirements.text: Extending a rating system to an additional business unit, product or obligor type, or to third-party-originated exposures is material, unless representativeness (CRR Art. 174(c)) and comparability (Art. 179(1)(d)) are demonstrated.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) No 529/2014, OJ L 148, 20.5.2014, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2015/942 (IRB provisions unchanged by that amendment). Annex I, Part I, Section 1, point 1(a)-(c) summarised; exact carve-outs differ per point. CRR3: EBA/RTS/2026/05 (final draft amending RTS under CRR Art. 143(5), 30.3.2026, not yet adopted in the OJ at time of authoring) replaces this with a single representativeness test and adds quantitative thresholds for extensions (new Art. 4(1)(d): 1.5% overall RWEA decrease or 15% RWEA increase). Re-verify once the amending Regulation is published.

requirements.text: A change is material if it decreases the overall credit and dilution risk RWEA by 1.5% at EU parent consolidated level (or at solo level for an institution that is neither parent nor subsidiary).
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) No 529/2014, OJ L 148, 20.5.2014, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2015/942 (IRB provisions unchanged by that amendment). The in-force text reads 'a decrease of 1,5 %' (no 'or more'); EBA/RTS/2026/05 reads '1,5 % or more'. Threshold unchanged.

requirements.text: A change is material if it decreases the credit and dilution risk RWEA associated with the range of application of the rating system by 15% or more.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) No 529/2014, OJ L 148, 20.5.2014, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2015/942 (IRB provisions unchanged by that amendment). EBA/RTS/2026/05 (final draft amending RTS under CRR3 Art. 143(5), 30.3.2026, not yet in the OJ) keeps the substance.

requirements.text: RWEA impact ratios are computed as the before/after RWEA difference over pre-change RWEA, at the same point in time, isolating the effect of the change and holding the exposure set constant.
requirements.quote: The determination of the impact on risk-weighted exposure amounts shall refer only to the impact of the change to the IRB approach
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) No 529/2014, OJ L 148, 20.5.2014, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2015/942 (IRB provisions unchanged by that amendment).

requirements.article: Reg. (EU) No 529/2014 Annex I, Part II, Section 1, point 3
requirements.text: Changes in the definition of default under CRR Art. 178 are classified as material.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) No 529/2014, OJ L 148, 20.5.2014, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2015/942 (IRB provisions unchanged by that amendment). CRR3: EBA/RTS/2026/05 (final draft amending RTS under CRR Art. 143(5), 30.3.2026, not yet adopted in the OJ at time of authoring) keeps only fundamental default-definition changes material (level of application for retail, or a significant change in default classifications measured against an institution-defined threshold). Re-verify once the amending Regulation is published.

requirements.article: Reg. (EU) No 529/2014 Annex I, Part II, Section 2, point 5(b)
requirements.text: A change of the data sources used for grade or pool assignment or for parameter estimation is notified ex ante.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) No 529/2014, OJ L 148, 20.5.2014, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2015/942 (IRB provisions unchanged by that amendment). CRR3: EBA/RTS/2026/05 (final draft amending RTS under CRR Art. 143(5), 30.3.2026, not yet adopted in the OJ at time of authoring) no longer lists data-source changes explicitly among ex ante items; only switches between internal, external and pooled data are material. Re-verify once the amending Regulation is published.

requirements.article: Reg. (EU) No 529/2014 Annex I, Part II, Section 2, point 5(c)
requirements.text: A change in the length or composition of the time series used for parameter estimation, beyond the annual inclusion of the latest observations, is notified ex ante.
requirements.verification_note: Checked against Reg. (EU) No 529/2014, OJ L 148, 20.5.2014, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2015/942 (IRB provisions unchanged by that amendment). EBA/RTS/2026/05 (final draft amending RTS under CRR3 Art. 143(5), 30.3.2026, not yet in the OJ) keeps the substance. See draft item (m) and new items (n)-(o) on calibration segments and sample.

requirements.text: The Tier 1 model is approved for use (gate G3) by the MRC, including its conditions of use.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The material change to a Tier 1 model, and every model change requiring supervisory permission, is approved by the MRC before submission to the ECB.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: Temporary use of a model with a Not fit for purpose opinion is approved only by the MRC and for at most six months.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The Tier 2 model or material change to it is approved by the Model Approval Panel, whose decision is reported to the MRC at its next meeting.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The approval decision states the approved scope of use, the underlying validation opinion, the open findings accepted and any conditions with owners and deadlines.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: Closure evidence for each condition is submitted before its deadline; closure of conditions related to validation findings is confirmed by Model Validation.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: Collateral data (type, value, valuation date and method, lien rank and link to the secured facilities) is recorded in the collateral system and meets the data quality requirements of MRM-STD-022.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to models that use collateral data.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy (CR-POL-001 v8.1) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Protected attributes are excluded and proxy variables are screened.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to models using data on natural persons or retail customers.
requirements.verification_note: Pilot requirement (kept verbatim); implemented by CR-POL-001 §9.2 (exclusion) and §9.3 (proxy screening).

requirements.text: Age is used in a credit model only where legally permitted and objectively justified by the credit characteristics of the product, with approval by Credit Risk Management and documentation.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to models using data on natural persons or retail customers.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy (CR-POL-001 v8.1) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: A variable identified as a potential proxy is used only with a documented credit-risk rationale and restricted to the minimum needed, for example aggregation of postcode to regional level.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to models using data on natural persons or retail customers.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy (CR-POL-001 v8.1) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The results of proxy screening and outcome testing are documented in the reference data set and model development documentation.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to models using data on natural persons or retail customers.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy (CR-POL-001 v8.1) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The model data is mapped to the data domains from which it is sourced.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §4.3.

requirements.text: The Model Owner has agreed with the relevant Data Owners the data quality expectations for the critical data elements used by the model.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §4.3.

requirements.text: Lineage from source systems to the RDS is documented for every variable.
requirements.verification_note: Pilot requirement (fixed id, text and article); DATA-POL-001 v3.2 §5.1 and §5.5.

requirements.text: Lineage from source systems to the production input data of the model is documented for every model variable, including discarded variables used to construct retained variables.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §5.1.

requirements.text: The lineage of each variable identifies the source system and fields, each intermediate data store, every transformation, filter, join and aggregation with a reference to the performing code or ETL job, and the extraction frequency and timing.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §5.2.

requirements.text: Manual interventions in the model data flow (manual uploads, end-user computing tools, manual corrections) are identified explicitly in the lineage together with the control applied to each.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §5.3.

requirements.text: For variables sourced from third parties or external data, the lineage starts at the point of receipt within the Bank and records the provider, the data product and the version or delivery date.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §5.4.

requirements.text: Lineage documentation reflects any change in source system, transformation logic or data flow before the changed data is used in development, monitoring or production.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §5.6.

requirements.text: The lineage of the development data and of the production input data is compared at implementation, and any difference in source or transformation is documented and its impact on the model assessed.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §5.7.

requirements.text: Every model input variable and every data element used to construct the target variable (including default flags, loss and recovery amounts and exposure at default) is designated as a critical data element.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §6.1.

requirements.text: Each critical data element has a documented business definition, a technical definition and at least one data quality rule for each applicable data quality dimension of MRM-STD-022 §3.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §6.2.

requirements.text: Critical data elements are reconciled against the source system or accounting data at least annually, and unexplained differences are recorded as data quality issues.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §6.3.

requirements.text: Metadata for every data element used in the model (business and technical definition, type and format, permitted values, unit and currency, source, Data Owner, update frequency, classification) is recorded in the Group Data Catalogue.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §7.1.

requirements.text: Where different definitions of the same concept are used (for example accounting and prudential default), each is labelled distinctly and the difference is documented.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §7.2.

requirements.text: Metadata changes are versioned so that the definition applicable to any historical data point in the model data can be retrieved.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §7.3.

requirements.text: Data quality of model data is managed in accordance with the Data Quality Standard for Models (MRM-STD-022).
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §8.1.

requirements.text: Data deficiencies identified in model data are remediated at source where feasible rather than corrected only in the model data.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §8.2.

requirements.text: Every data quality issue affecting a critical data element of the model is recorded in the Bank data issue register and in the model's data deficiency log with impact, owner, remediation plan and target date.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §8.3.

requirements.text: Data quality issues rated high or critical that affect a model are escalated to the Group Data Governance Committee and to the Model Risk Committee.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §8.4.

requirements.text: Model data is aggregated on a largely automated basis; remaining manual processes are documented, justified and controlled.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §9.2.

requirements.text: Data used for model outputs feeding regulatory capital or risk reporting is reconcilable with the Bank's accounting data and with the data used in the corresponding regulatory reports.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to models whose outputs feed regulatory capital or risk reporting.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §9.3.

requirements.text: Personal data in model data sets is not retained longer than necessary for the purpose, in accordance with PRIV-POL-001.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to models processing personal data only.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §10.1.

requirements.text: Each RDS version used for development or recalibration is archived together with the code used to construct it and its lineage and metadata, so that the development data can be reproduced.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §10.2.

requirements.text: Archived RDS versions are retained for the life of the model and at least ten years after its decommissioning.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §10.2.

requirements.text: Historical data required for risk parameter estimation (rating histories, default events, loss and recovery cash flows, exposure histories) is retained for at least the observation periods required by CRR Articles 176, 180 and 181.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to IRB models used for own funds requirements only.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §10.3.

requirements.text: Archived model data is protected against alteration, and any correction is made on a new version with the original retained.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §10.4.

requirements.text: Any deviation from DATA-POL-001 affecting model data is covered by a dispensation approved by the Chief Data Officer and the Head of Model Risk Management, with an expiry date of at most twelve months.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (DATA-POL-001 v3.2), §12.1.

requirements.text: The model is managed under the Model Risk Management Policy irrespective of whether it is developed internally, acquired from a vendor, provided by a group entity or operated as a service by a third party.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: A 1LoD model owner is accountable for use of the model within its approved scope, the accuracy of its inventory record, ongoing monitoring, remediation of findings and fulfilment of approval conditions.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The model developer develops the model in accordance with MRM-STD-020 and documents it in accordance with MRM-STD-021.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The new model or material model change passes the lifecycle gates G0 (registration), G1 (development sign-off), G2 (validation), G3 (approval for use) and G4 (go-live) with the evidence and approver specified for each gate.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: No gate is passed before all preceding gates are completed, and each gate decision and its supporting evidence are recorded in the model inventory.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: Before submission to Model Validation, the model developer completes a self-assessment against the applicable requirement set from the requirement library, with an evidence reference for each requirement.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The model is decommissioned only with the approval of the approval authority for its tier, and its inventory record and documentation are retained for at least ten years.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The model is registered in the model inventory before its development starts and in any case before its output is used.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The model is assigned a tier (1, 2 or 3) based on materiality and complexity, subject to the minimum tiers for regulatory use in MRM-STD-010.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The model and its material changes are approved for use by the authority for its tier: the MRC for Tier 1, the Model Approval Panel for Tier 2 and the Head of Model Risk Management for Tier 3.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The approval decision is based on the validation opinion, the 1LoD self-assessment, open findings, known limitations and proposed post-model adjustments, and records any conditions.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: Internal approval (G3) precedes the application to the ECB, and the model is used to calculate own funds requirements only after supervisory permission has been granted.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to internal models requiring supervisory permission (IRB rating systems and market risk IMA) only.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: A model with a Not fit for purpose validation opinion is not approved for use.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The model is independently validated before first use and after every material change.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The model is validated periodically at the frequency for its tier (Tier 1 annually, Tier 2 every two years, Tier 3 every three years), and at least annually if used for own funds requirements.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: Validation of a vendor or third-party model is not waived for lack of transparency; the model owner obtains documentation sufficient for validation or MRM-approved compensating controls are in place.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.chapter: Use of models with open findings
requirements.text: A model with a Not fit for purpose opinion is not used, except for MRC-approved temporary use of at most six months with compensating measures and an approved remediation plan.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.chapter: Use of models with open findings
requirements.text: A model with a Fit for purpose with conditions opinion is used only subject to its conditions, each recorded in the MRC conditions register with an owner and a deadline.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.chapter: Use of models with open findings
requirements.text: For every open high- or medium-severity finding, the model owner submits a remediation plan within 20 business days of the final validation report.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: Before gate G1, the model inventory records whether the model is or is part of an AI system and, if so, its risk classification under the AI Act.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: Any deviation from the Policy or an MRM standard for the model is covered by an approved, time-bound dispensation that states the rationale, risk assessment, compensating measures and end date.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The purposes of processing personal data in the model are specified, explicit and recorded in the Record of Processing.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (PRIV-POL-001 v4.0); GDPR article references checked.

requirements.text: Where personal data collected for another purpose are reused for model development, a documented compatibility assessment under Art. 6(4) GDPR or a separate lawful basis exists.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (PRIV-POL-001 v4.0); GDPR article references checked.

requirements.text: Every personal data attribute used in the model is justified by its relevance to the model purpose (data minimisation).
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (PRIV-POL-001 v4.0); GDPR article references checked.

requirements.text: The processing of personal data for the model has a documented lawful basis under Art. 6(1) GDPR recorded before processing starts.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (PRIV-POL-001 v4.0); GDPR article references checked.

requirements.text: Where legitimate interests are relied upon, a documented legitimate interest assessment demonstrates purpose, necessity and balancing against data subjects' rights.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (PRIV-POL-001 v4.0); GDPR article references checked.

requirements.article: PRIV-POL-001 §5.3; GDPR Art. 9; AI Act Art. 10(5)
requirements.text: Special categories of personal data are not used for model development or scoring unless an Art. 9(2) GDPR exception applies and the Privacy Office has approved it, or, for bias detection in high-risk AI, Art. 10(5) AI Act conditions are met.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (PRIV-POL-001 v4.0); GDPR article references checked.

requirements.text: The model is linked to its processing activities in the Record of Processing, and the Model Inventory or AI Inventory records that reference.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (PRIV-POL-001 v4.0); GDPR article references checked.

requirements.text: A DPIA is performed before processing for every model that scores or classifies natural persons for decisions, uses ML or generative AI on personal data, or is Tier 1.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (PRIV-POL-001 v4.0); GDPR article references checked.

requirements.text: The DPIA describes the processing and purposes, assesses necessity and proportionality and the risks to data subjects, and sets out the mitigating measures.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (PRIV-POL-001 v4.0); GDPR article references checked.

requirements.text: The DPO's advice on the DPIA is documented, and residual high risk triggers prior consultation of the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens before processing.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (PRIV-POL-001 v4.0); GDPR article references checked.

requirements.text: The DPIA is reviewed on every material change, including new personal data attributes in a new model version, and at least every three years.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (PRIV-POL-001 v4.0).

requirements.text: Model development and validation use pseudonymised data, with direct identifiers replaced by keyed tokens whose keys are held by a separate data custodian, unless identifying data are approved by the Privacy Office.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (PRIV-POL-001 v4.0); GDPR article references checked.

requirements.text: Re-identification of pseudonymised development data occurs only for a documented, Privacy Office-approved purpose and is logged.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (PRIV-POL-001 v4.0).

requirements.text: Development data sets containing personal data are held only in approved secure analytics environments with role-based access.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (PRIV-POL-001 v4.0); GDPR article references checked.

requirements.text: Production personal data are used in test environments only when masked, pseudonymised or replaced by synthetic data, unless approved by the Privacy Office.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (PRIV-POL-001 v4.0).

requirements.text: The RDS documentation lists the personal data attributes used, their purpose in the model, the lawful basis, the pseudonymisation applied and the retention period.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (PRIV-POL-001 v4.0).

requirements.text: Reference data sets and development snapshots containing personal data are retained no longer than the model's period of use plus five years after decommissioning, unless approved by the Privacy Office.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (PRIV-POL-001 v4.0); GDPR article references checked.

requirements.text: At the end of the retention period personal data are deleted or irreversibly anonymised, and deletion is evidenced.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (PRIV-POL-001 v4.0); GDPR article references checked.

requirements.text: Transfers of personal data outside the EEA, including to third-party AI services, are based on an adequacy decision or appropriate safeguards and a documented transfer impact assessment.
requirements.verification_note: Internal policy text authored for the library (PRIV-POL-001 v4.0); GDPR article references checked.

requirements.text: Every planned model change is recorded in the change log of the model inventory before implementation in production.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The change memorandum describes the change and rationale, affected components and documents, internal and regulatory classification with analysis, quantitative impact, required validation and implementation plan.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: Related changes planned together or addressing the same deficiency are recorded and assessed as a single change.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: Every change is classified by internal materiality and, for models requiring supervisory permission, by regulatory class (A, B or C).
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: A change is classified as internally material if it alters methodology, drivers, default or target definition, range of application or use, introduces a new material input source, or exceeds the output-impact thresholds of §5.2(e).
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The change impact on aggregate model output at the most recent reference date and on grade or class assignments is quantified against the 5% and 10% thresholds.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The regulatory class follows Delegated Regulation 529/2014: Class A if a qualitative material-change criterion is met or RWEA decreases by at least 1.5% overall or 15% in the range of application.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to internal models requiring supervisory permission (IRB rating systems and market risk IMA) only.
requirements.verification_note: Internal provision implementing Delegated Regulation (EU) No 529/2014. Thresholds and criteria restated from knowledge of the RTS (Art. 4 and Annex I); verify against EUR-Lex and check whether a CRR3 successor RTS under CRR Art. 143(5) applies.

requirements.text: The quantitative impact is calculated on the same most recent reference date before and after the change, at Bank-wide RWEA level and at the level of the rating system’s range of application.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to internal models requiring supervisory permission (IRB rating systems and market risk IMA) only.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: Changes are not split, sequenced or combined to avoid a higher classification, and the cumulative impact of changes since the last permission or full validation is assessed.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The change classification proposed by the model developer is approved by MRM, with disagreements escalated to the MRC.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: Where the classification is uncertain, the higher internal materiality or regulatory class is applied.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: Every internally material change is independently validated before implementation.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: A Class A or Class B change is validated before the application or ex ante notification is submitted, and the validation report is part of the submission.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to internal models requiring supervisory permission (IRB rating systems and market risk IMA) only.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: For a non-material change to a Tier 1 model, Model Validation decides within ten business days whether a review before implementation is required.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: A re-validation is triggered by an unresolved red monitoring outcome, a material change in portfolio composition or external environment, a relevant regulatory change or a change in intended use.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The next validation is full-scope where cumulative non-material changes since the last full validation together meet the internal materiality criteria.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: An internally material change passes gates G1 to G4 and is approved by the authority for the model tier; a Class A change is approved by the MRC before submission.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: A non-material change is approved by the model owner after MRM has confirmed its classification, and the new model version is recorded in the inventory.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: A Class A change is used to calculate own funds requirements only after the ECB has granted permission.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to internal models requiring supervisory permission (IRB rating systems and market risk IMA) only.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: ECB obligations, limitations and recommendations attached to a permission are recorded in the inventory with owner and deadline and tracked as MRC conditions.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to internal models requiring supervisory permission (IRB rating systems and market risk IMA) only.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: Data, code and documentation supporting the application remain available, and the RDS and model estimation remain reproducible, throughout the ECB assessment.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to internal models requiring supervisory permission (IRB rating systems and market risk IMA) only.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: A post-implementation review comparing realised with estimated impact is performed within six months of implementing an internally material change and reported to MRM.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The applicable requirement set is derived from the requirement library at the start of development and used to plan evidence and documentation.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The RDS is signed off by the model owner before model estimation starts, and material RDS changes after sign-off are signed off again.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: Sensitivity analyses cover key assumptions, parameters and input data of a Tier 1 or Tier 2 model, including alternative exclusions, target definitions, calibration windows and expert judgements.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The impact of every material expert judgement is quantified through sensitivity analysis.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: Development code is reviewed by a second developer who did not write it before results are submitted to Model Validation.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: Sign-offs of the development plan, the RDS and the final model by the model owner (and, for the final model, the head of the modelling unit) are recorded in the model inventory.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The model is submitted to Model Validation only after gate G1 has been passed.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.chapter: Documentation template, version control and approval
requirements.text: The document follows the RDS template and is version-controlled with approvals.
requirements.verification_note: Pilot requirement (fixed ID, text and article). Covers §2.2–2.8 for the RDS documentation template of Annex A.

requirements.chapter: Documentation template, version control and approval
requirements.text: The model has RDS documentation per Annex A, an MDD per Annex B, an implementation specification per MRM-STD-030 and a monitoring plan per MRM-STD-040.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.chapter: Documentation template, version control and approval
requirements.text: A template section that does not apply is retained with the statement "Not applicable" and a justification, and added sections do not alter template numbering.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.chapter: Documentation template, version control and approval
requirements.text: The document carries a cover block with title, model identifier and version, document version, status, author, reviewer, approver and approval date.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.chapter: Documentation template, version control and approval
requirements.text: The document is stored in the controlled document repository linked to the model inventory and contains a document history table with version, date, change summary, author and approver.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.chapter: Documentation template, version control and approval
requirements.text: The document is reviewed before approval by a qualified reviewer who is not its author, and the review is recorded in the document history.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.chapter: Documentation template, version control and approval
requirements.text: The RDS documentation is approved by the model owner after data quality sign-off, and the MDD by the model owner and the head of the modelling unit.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.chapter: Documentation template, version control and approval
requirements.text: Only approved document versions are submitted to Model Validation, the approval authority and supervisors.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.chapter: Documentation template, version control and approval
requirements.text: An approved document version is never overwritten; any change results in a new version that is reviewed and approved.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The RDS documentation describes the construction and data quality of the RDS in sufficient detail for Model Validation to rebuild the RDS independently from source data.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The RDS build is reproducible from versioned code.
requirements.verification_note: Pilot requirement (fixed ID, text and article).

requirements.text: No manual data manipulation is used in the RDS build; unavoidable manual inputs are version-controlled files documented as expert judgement under MRM-STD-023.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The RDS documentation records the repository, build code tag, source snapshot reference dates and the result of a full rebuild compared with the frozen RDS (row count and default or target event count).
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The frozen RDS is stored read-only with a version identifier that is referenced in both the RDS documentation and the MDD.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The RDS documentation contains a data dictionary stating for every RDS variable its business definition, source system and field, and transformation.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: Every data deficiency in section 6.2 of the RDS documentation has an identifier and is cross-referenced to the MDD limitations log.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The RDS documentation states the observation period with start and end dates, snapshot frequency, number of observations, unique facilities or obligors, and number of defaults or target events.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The default definition section states the level of application (obligor or facility) and describes any historical approximation of the default flag.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to credit risk models with a default-based target only.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The exclusions section states, for each exclusion, the conclusion of the impact analysis with a reference to section 5.3.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: The RDS documentation, the MDD, the implementation specification and the production code are consistent with each other.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: Every evidence reference in the 1LoD self-assessment points to a section number of an approved document version.
requirements.verification_note: Internal document authored for the library; requirement derived from the cited numbered provision.

requirements.text: Default is identified at obligor level for all exposure classes, and all credit obligations of a defaulted obligor are flagged as defaulted.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Joint credit obligations and contagion between connected obligors are treated in accordance with section 8 of EBA/GL/2016/07.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The date of default is the first day on which any default criterion is met and is recorded for every default event.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Days past due are counted from the first day on which both the absolute and the relative materiality components are exceeded, and reset when either is no longer exceeded.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The materiality threshold is EUR 100 and 1% for retail exposures and EUR 500 and 1% for non-retail exposures.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text; thresholds consistent with RTS 2018/171 and pilot REQ-D07 (retail EUR 100 / 1%).

requirements.text: The absolute component is compared with the sum of all past due amounts of the obligor, and the relative component is that sum divided by the obligor's total on-balance-sheet exposure.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Where the repayment schedule is changed, days past due are counted on the modified schedule, and forbearance changes are assessed for distressed restructuring.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Technical past due is recognised only in the situations defined as technical past due in EBA/GL/2016/07, and each case is documented and corrected within 30 days.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Non-accrued status, specific credit risk adjustments (including Stage 3), sale at a credit-related loss above 5%, distressed restructuring with DFO above 1%, bankruptcy and forced sale of collateral lead to default automatically.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text; triggers consistent with CRR Art. 178(3) and EBA/GL/2016/07 section 5, and with the UTP triggers of the pilot RDS.

requirements.text: Additional UTP indicators (such as fraud, significant income or cash-flow decline, covenant breach, multiple forbearance) lead to a case-by-case assessment completed within 30 days of detection.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Each UTP trigger and indicator is mapped to source-system fields, and the outcome of each case-by-case assessment is recorded with its rationale.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The diminished financial obligation is calculated as the relative reduction in net present value of expected cash flows caused by the restructuring, discounted at the original effective interest rate.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: An obligor returns to non-default status only after at least three months without any default trigger and an assessment that the improvement in credit quality is factual and permanent.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: After a distressed restructuring, the probation period is at least 12 months, and return requires a material payment, no amount past due and no concerns about full repayment.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The probation start date and status are recorded for every default event.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Where an obligor defaults again within 12 months of returning to non-default status, both events are treated as a single default starting on the first date of default for risk parameter estimation.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The RDS identifies and links multiple default events, and the number of merged default events is reported in the RDS documentation.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The RDS default flag is constructed in accordance with CR-STD-110, including materiality thresholds, UTP triggers, probation periods and the treatment of multiple defaults.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The default flag construction in the RDS code is reconciled with the production default flag for the periods in which both are available, and differences are explained.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: For periods before 1 January 2016 the approximation of the default flag from arrears and restructuring data is documented and its effect on default rates quantified.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Periods for which the default flag could not be reconstructed with probation periods are stated in the RDS documentation together with the treatment applied.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Data quality is assessed on completeness, accuracy, consistency and timeliness.
requirements.verification_note: Pilot requirement (fixed id, text and article); MRM-STD-022 v2.2 §3.1. BCBS 239 principles 3 (accuracy and integrity), 4 (completeness), 5 (timeliness).

requirements.text: Completeness of model data is measured at record level (all in-scope obligors, facilities, defaults and recoveries included) and at attribute level (share of non-missing values per variable).
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §3.2.

requirements.text: Accuracy of model data is measured by reconciliation to source systems or accounting data, comparison with independent sources, and sample-based checks against source documentation.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §3.3.

requirements.text: Consistency is assessed between the RDS and production input data, over the observation period (including changes in default definition), and as logical consistency between related fields.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §3.4.

requirements.text: Timeliness is measured as the lag between reference date and data availability and as the currency of periodically refreshed items such as financial statements and collateral values.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §3.5.

requirements.text: Validity, uniqueness and appropriateness (representativeness for the model's range of application) of the model data are assessed where relevant to the model.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §3.6.

requirements.text: For every critical data element of the model at least one DQ rule is defined for each applicable mandatory dimension, and the reason is recorded where a dimension is not applicable.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §4.1.

requirements.text: The DQ rules for the model's critical data elements are documented in the RDS documentation and recurring checks are implemented in the Group DQ monitoring tool.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §4.2.

requirements.text: Each DQ rule has an amber and a red threshold, at least as strict as the default thresholds of MRM-STD-022 §4.3 unless a justified deviation is approved.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §4.3.

requirements.text: DQ thresholds for the target variable and its constituents (default flag, default date, realised loss, recovery cash flows, exposure at default) are at least as strict as the default thresholds.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §4.4.

requirements.text: Accuracy of the default flag in the model data is confirmed by reconciliation of default events to the default register maintained under CR-STD-110.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to credit risk models with a default-based target variable.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §4.4.

requirements.text: Deviations from the default DQ thresholds are justified in the RDS documentation and approved by the Model Owner, and for less strict thresholds on Tier 1 models also by Model Risk Management.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §4.5.

requirements.text: A documented DQ assessment is performed on the RDS before development, on every new RDS version used for recalibration, and on the data used for each periodic validation.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §5.1.

requirements.text: The DQ assessment reports the result of each DQ rule per variable and dimension against its thresholds, and the number and share of records excluded from the RDS by reason of exclusion.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §5.2.

requirements.text: Every exclusion of records from the RDS is justified, quantified and assessed for its effect on representativeness; exclusions above 5% of records or exposure in any segment are approved by the Model Owner and reported to Model Validation.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §5.3.

requirements.text: The RDS is reconciled to source systems or accounting data for key amounts (exposure, outstanding balance, losses) and for record counts per reference date.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §5.4.

requirements.text: For Tier 1 models the DQ assessment includes sample-based verification of accuracy against source documentation such as credit files and collateral valuations.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §5.5.

requirements.text: The DQ assessment concludes explicitly whether the data is fit for the intended use and is signed off by the model developer and the Model Owner before the RDS is frozen.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §5.6.

requirements.text: The DQ rules applied to the RDS are also applied to the production input data of the model.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §5.7.

requirements.text: The treatment of missing values is documented per variable, distinguishing values missing at random, missing for a structural reason and missing because of a data deficiency.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §6.1.

requirements.text: Imputation of missing values uses a documented, reproducible method; the share of imputed values per variable is reported and the effect of imputation on estimated parameters is assessed.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §6.2.

requirements.text: Outliers are identified using documented criteria applied consistently between development and production.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §6.3.

requirements.text: The treatment of outliers (correction, capping, flooring, exclusion) is justified, applied consistently between development and production, and its impact on the model output quantified.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §6.4.

requirements.text: Missing values and outliers in the target variable are not imputed; affected records are investigated and corrected at source or excluded with justification.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §6.5.

requirements.text: The model has a data deficiency log recording each identified deficiency with affected variables and segments, DQ dimension, cause, quantified or estimated impact and treatment.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §7.1.

requirements.text: Each data deficiency is treated by remediation at source, evidenced correction, exclusion, methodological adjustment or recognition in the margin of conservatism, and the treatment is documented.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §7.2.

requirements.article: MRM-STD-022 §7.3; CRR Art. 179(1)(f); EBA/GL/2017/16 (margin of conservatism)
requirements.text: Each data deficiency not fully remediated is assessed for inclusion in the margin of conservatism as a category A deficiency under CRM-STD-101, and the log references the MoC component it is mapped to.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to IRB models used for own funds requirements only.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §7.3.

requirements.text: Corrections of model data not supported by documented source evidence are treated as expert judgement and documented and approved under MRM-STD-023.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §7.4.

requirements.text: Each data deficiency has a remediation owner and target date, is closed only on confirmed remediation, and the related MoC component is then reassessed.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §7.5.

requirements.text: Red DQ threshold breaches on a critical data element of a Tier 1 model are escalated to Model Risk Management within ten business days and reported to the Model Risk Committee.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-022 v2.2), §8.3.

requirements.chapter: Documentation and approval of expert judgement
requirements.text: Expert judgement applied in data treatment is documented and approved.
requirements.verification_note: Pilot requirement (fixed id, text and article); MRM-STD-023 v1.4 §2.1–2.2, with data treatment types in §3.1.

requirements.chapter: Documentation and approval of expert judgement
requirements.text: The model has an expert judgement log, stored with the model documentation, in which every instance of expert judgement is recorded with its type, life cycle stage and affected data, segment or parameter.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-023 v1.4), §2.2.

requirements.chapter: Documentation and approval of expert judgement
requirements.text: Each expert judgement log entry records the rationale, the evidence relied on and the alternatives considered and rejected.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-023 v1.4), §2.2(d).

requirements.chapter: Documentation and approval of expert judgement
requirements.text: Each expert judgement log entry records the quantified impact on the model output, or a qualitative assessment with the reason quantification is not possible.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-023 v1.4), §2.2(e).

requirements.chapter: Documentation and approval of expert judgement
requirements.text: Each expert judgement log entry records the proposer, the approver and the date of approval.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-023 v1.4), §2.2(g)-(h).

requirements.chapter: Documentation and approval of expert judgement
requirements.text: Each expert judgement log entry records a review date and the conditions under which the judgement expires.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-023 v1.4), §2.2(i).

requirements.chapter: Documentation and approval of expert judgement
requirements.text: The rationale for each expert judgement is specific enough for a knowledgeable third party to understand it and replicate its effect; unsupported references to business experience are not sufficient.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-023 v1.4), §2.3.

requirements.chapter: Documentation and approval of expert judgement
requirements.text: Expert judgement is approved at the level set by its materiality: Model Owner (low), Model Owner and head of development (medium), Model Risk Committee after Model Validation review (high).
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-023 v1.4), §2.4.

requirements.chapter: Documentation and approval of expert judgement
requirements.text: The proposer of an expert judgement is not its sole approver.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-023 v1.4), §2.5.

requirements.chapter: Documentation and approval of expert judgement
requirements.text: The expert judgement log is referenced in the MDD and, for judgements in data treatment, in the RDS documentation.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-023 v1.4), §2.7.

requirements.chapter: Documentation and approval of expert judgement
requirements.text: Each expert judgement is reviewed at least at each annual model review and when new data could replace it, and withdrawn judgements are recorded in the log.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-023 v1.4), §2.8.

requirements.text: Expert judgement in data treatment that addresses a data deficiency is cross-referenced to the data deficiency log of MRM-STD-022.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-023 v1.4), §3.2.

requirements.text: Expert judgement in data treatment addressing a data deficiency is linked to the assessment of the related margin of conservatism under CRM-STD-101.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to IRB models used for own funds requirements only.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-023 v1.4), §3.2.

requirements.text: Each expert judgement is classified as low, medium or high materiality based on its impact on the model output relative to the output without the judgement or the best statistical alternative.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-023 v1.4), §4.1.

requirements.text: Expert judgement whose impact cannot be quantified is classified as at least medium materiality, and as high materiality for Tier 1 models.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-023 v1.4), §4.4.

requirements.text: Every expert judgement of medium or high materiality is subject to documented challenge by a person independent of the proposer before approval, with the challenge and resolution recorded in the log.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-023 v1.4), §5.1.

requirements.text: The implementation specification defines the production source field and lineage of every input variable and identifies any difference between development and production data sources.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-030 v2.0), §4.2.

requirements.text: The MDD records the development code version, RDS version and parameter set that produced the reported results.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-030 v2.0), §5.2.

requirements.text: Production outputs are reconciled at record level with development code outputs on identical input data covering the full RDS or at least 10,000 records per segment.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-030 v2.0), §8.1.

requirements.text: The lineage of development data and production input data is compared and the effect of any difference on model outputs is quantified.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-030 v2.0), §8.4.

requirements.text: The model is used in production only after implementation testing, reconciliation, parallel run where required and UAT are completed and the model is approved for use under MRM-POL-001.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-030 v2.0), §10.1.

requirements.text: Production input data is subject to completeness and validity checks applying the DQ rules of MRM-STD-022.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text authored for the library (MRM-STD-030 v2.0), §10.2.
